canonical_audit_reconstruction.text:
Let E be an arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its normed additive group structure and its Borel measurable structure. Dimension zero is allowed. Let V:E→ℝ be twice continuously Fréchet differentiable. Let α,β be nonnegative real numbers and η a real number. Assume α>0, α≤β, η>0, βη≤1, and, for every x,v∈E,
  α‖v‖² ≤ (D(DV)(x)[v])[v] ≤ β‖v‖².
Here α and β in real formulas denote their real coercions. There are no other assumptions on V or on the initial/reference points.

Fix any y,xRef∈E, initial phase point z₀∈E×E, and n∈ℕ. The functions below also exist before these points and n are fixed. Write a phase point as z=(x,v). Put g(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(xRef) and c=y−η∇V(xRef). For every real t define
  Φ(t,(x,v))=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+√η sin(t)v,
              −sin(t)/√η (x−c)+cos(t)v).
Define
  S(x,v)=(x,v−[2⟨v,g(x)⟩/‖g(x)‖²]g(x)),
  λ(x,v)=√η max(0,⟨v,g(x)⟩).
All products with vectors are real scalar multiplication. Division is total with division by zero equal to zero; in particular S(x,v)=(x,v) whenever g(x)=0. The flow Φ is defined on all real times, including negative times. For t∈ℝ≥0 define the real interval Bochner integral
  Λ(z,t)=∫₀ᵗ λ(Φ(s,z)) ds.
For e∈ℝ≥0 define the extended nonnegative waiting time
  τ(z,e)=inf{t∈ℝ≥0 : Λ(z,t)−e≥0} ∈ [0,∞],
where the infimum of the empty hitting set is ∞, with the hitting search starting at time 0. The target is the closed nonnegative half-line, so equality Λ=e is included. Write τ₀(z,e) for τ(z,e) when finite and for 0 when τ(z,e)=∞. This is the literal untopD 0 default, not a claim that an infinite wait is a zero waiting event.

The tagged record space is Rec=(ℝ≥0×(E×E)) ⊔ {†}. Denote its two distinct tags by live(a,z) and †. A live record contains cumulative time a≥0 and a phase point z. The singleton tag has no such data. For an input e≥0 define
  next(e,†)=†;
  next(e,live(a,z))=† if τ(z,e)=∞;
  next(e,live(a,z))=live(a+τ₀(z,e), S(Φ(τ₀(z,e),z))) otherwise.
For any sequence e:ℕ→ℝ≥0, the finite recursion starts at r₀(e)=live(0,z₀) and sets rₖ₊₁(e)=next(eₖ,rₖ(e)). Once † occurs it persists.

The underlying sample space is Ω=ℝ^ℕ, with P the canonical countable product of rate-one exponential probability laws on ℝ. For every w∈Ω define εₖ(w)=max(wₖ,0)∈ℝ≥0 and Rₖ(w)=rₖ(ε(w)). These definitions apply to every real sequence, not just to sequences in the almost-sure support of P. Put Hist=Rec^{0,…,n} and HistNext=Rec^{0,…,n+1}. Define H(w)=(R₀(w),…,Rₙ(w)) and Hnext(w)=(R₀(w),…,Rₙ₊₁(w)). In particular H includes the entire finite record tuple through stage n, with its tags. Products and finite function spaces carry the indicated Borel structures. Define readTime(live(a,z))=a as a real number and readTime(†)=0. For any h∈Hist define a(h)=readTime(hₙ), and for any w∈Ω define U(w)=readTime(Rₙ₊₁(w)). Thus U is the cumulative time of a live next record and is zero for a next record tagged †.

For r∈Rec and q∈ℝ define three observations. The extended wait is
  W(live(a,z),q)=τ(z,max(q,0)),  W(†,q)=0.
Its real-valued version T(r,q) is W(r,q) coerced to a real number when finite, and is zero when W(r,q)=∞. In particular T(†,q)=0. The nonnegative extended density observation is
  ρ(live(a,z),t)=ofReal( λ(Φ(t,z)) exp(−Λ(z,max(t,0))) ),
  ρ(†,t)=0,
for every real t. Here ofReal(r)=max(r,0), embedded into [0,∞]. The stored cumulative time a is ignored by W and ρ. In the formula for ρ, the flow uses the raw real t whereas the integrated rate uses max(t,0). These inputs must not be identified for negative t.

For h∈Hist and s∈ℝ define appendRel(h,s) to be the tuple h followed by
  live(q+max(s,0), S(Φ(s,z))) if hₙ=live(q,z),
  † if hₙ=†.
The flow again uses the raw real s, while the appended time uses max(s,0). Define
  appendAbs(h,u)=appendRel(h,u−a(h)),
  liftAbs(h,u)=(appendAbs(h,u),u).
These maps are defined for every h and every u∈ℝ, including h not arising from the recursion and u≤a(h). The first n+1 coordinates of appendAbs(h,u) are exactly h.

The proposition asserts that H, Hnext, a, U, appendAbs and liftAbs are Borel measurable, and that, for every (h,u)∈Hist×ℝ and every j∈{0,…,n}, the jth old coordinate of appendAbs(h,u) is hⱼ.

In addition, for EVERY Borel measurable function b:Hist→ℝ≥0, make the following definitions. This is an arbitrary cutoff depending on the whole history, not necessarily a constant, a function only of its last coordinate, or a bound beyond its current cumulative time. Let
  d(h)=max(b(h)−a(h),0)∈ℝ≥0,
  μ=H_*P.
For all h∈Hist and u∈ℝ set
  D(h,u)=ρ(hₙ,u−a(h)) if a(h)<u<b(h),
  D(h,u)=0 otherwise.
Both inequalities are strict. In particular when hₙ=live(q,z), the density on that interval is
  ofReal(λ(Φ(u−q,z)) exp(−Λ(z,max(u−q,0))));
when hₙ=† it is zero everywhere. This definition and the forthcoming fiber bound apply to every h, even histories not in the image or support of H.

Define events
  Brel={w : 0<W(Rₙ(w),wₙ)<d(H(w))},
where these comparisons take place in the extended nonnegative reals and the finite d is embedded there, and
  B={w : Rₙ(w) has the live tag, Rₙ₊₁(w) has the live tag,
           a(H(w))<U(w)<b(H(w))}.
The explicit live requirements cannot be replaced by inequalities using the zero-valued time defaults alone. Define X(w)=(H(w),U(w)), Y(w)=(Hnext(w),U(w)), and the measure ν on Hist×ℝ by
  ν=(μ⊗Lebesgue).withDensity((h,u)↦D(h,u)).
Thus ν integrates the displayed nonnegative density against the history law and ordinary real Lebesgue measure.

For each such b the proposition asserts all of the following simultaneously:
1. D is jointly Borel measurable. For EVERY h∈Hist,
     ∫_[ℝ] D(h,u) du ≤ 1,
   where this is a nonnegative extended Lebesgue integral.
2. B is measurable; X and Y are measurable; and Brel=B as exact sets, with no almost-everywhere qualification.
3. For EVERY w∈B,
     U(w)=a(H(w))+T(Rₙ(w),wₙ),
     Hnext(w)=appendAbs(X(w)).
4. The following are equalities of measures:
     X_*(P restricted to B)=ν,
     Y_*(P restricted to B)=(liftAbs)_*ν,
     (Hnext)_*(P restricted to B)=(appendAbs)_*ν.
   Also ν(Hist×ℝ)≤1. Restrictions are unnormalized. In particular the first measure identity implies ν(Hist×ℝ)=P(B); the formula is valid also when P(B)=0. It does not divide by P(B) or assert that ν is a probability measure.
5. For EVERY Borel measurable G:Hist×ℝ→[0,∞], the function
     h↦∫_[ℝ] G(h,u)D(h,u) du
   is measurable, and for EVERY Borel A⊆Hist,
     ∫_[B∩H⁻¹(A)] G(X(w)) P(dw)
       =∫_[A] [∫_[ℝ] G(h,u)D(h,u) du] μ(dh).
6. For EVERY Borel measurable F:HistNext×ℝ→[0,∞], the function
     h↦∫_[ℝ] F(liftAbs(h,u))D(h,u) du
   is measurable, and for EVERY Borel A⊆Hist,
     ∫_[B∩H⁻¹(A)] F(Y(w)) P(dw)
       =∫_[A] [∫_[ℝ] F(liftAbs(h,u))D(h,u) du] μ(dh).
   Expanding liftAbs, the test function on the right is F(appendAbs(h,u),u).

All integrals in items 1 and 5–6 and the withDensity construction take values in the extended nonnegative reals. G and F may take the value ∞ and no integrability or boundedness assumption is imposed; equality remains meaningful even when both sides are ∞. Products use extended-nonnegative arithmetic, in particular 0·∞=∞·0=0. Hence a zero density contributes zero even for an infinite test value. Null restrictions integrate every nonnegative extended test function to zero. No conditional probability on a positive-probability history event is needed: A is arbitrary measurable, and μ(A)=0 is permitted. The cutoff may satisfy b(h)≤a(h), in which case the interval at that h is empty and d(h)=0. Zero waits, infinite waits, and waits ending exactly at the upper cutoff are excluded by Brel; the assertion does not claim they are impossible for every input. The pointwise recursions and event equality include input sequences of P-measure zero, including coordinates that are negative or zero. There is no assertion of global non-explosion, eventual finiteness of each wait, normalization of each density fiber to one, stationarity, or a source-equivalence verdict. This is a statement at each finite index n with the displayed restrictions.
